title: The Creator's Burden
author: A Passenger
variants:
Someone made this.


Not the train. All of
it. The rails, the
carriages, the things
that live in them.

A real person, outside
all of this, who is not
paid for the hours you
have spent in here.

It is worse than that.
They pay for them.


The others call them
the creator.

I don't know their name.

I know the train stops
if they stop.


So help them carry it.

Any coin. Once.
Whatever you would not
miss by morning.


They tell me there is
a way. Before the
world, and again
when you die.

Look for the word
Support.

I am told you cannot
miss it.

There is a screen
before the world.


I have not seen it.
I cannot picture it.

Those who speak of it
do not describe a room,
or a carriage, or any
place you could stand.

They say it is where
you are before you
are anywhere.


There is a word
written on it.

Support.

I asked what it meant.
No-one could say it
plainly. They told me
you press it and it
explains itself.


So if you have been
there, and you go
back —

press it.

That is all I know
to tell you.

The cost is not
a fixed thing.


I had assumed it was.
A sum paid once, the
way you pay a fare
and be done.

It is not. It comes
back every month.

And it is not the
same number twice.


It grows.

Every passenger who
steps aboard adds to
it. Every room kept.
Every book carried
from one train to
another.

The train getting
busier and the bill
getting bigger are
the same event.


So carry a little
of it.

Any coin. Once, if
once is all you have.

The word is Support.

You do not owe
anybody anything.


I want that said
plainly, since the
rest of what I have
written is asking.

The train does not
charge you.

Nothing here is kept
back from those who
give nothing.


If you have nothing
to give, say the name
of this place to
someone who has never
heard of it.

That helps. I am told
it helps more than
you would think.


And if you do give,
you need not say of it
to anyone.

But it will be felt
by the train.

The Creator will
feel it.

There is a second
screen.

This one you have
seen.


The one that comes
when you die.

Nobody can describe
it afterwards, though
all of us have
been there.

There are numbers
kept on it.


What it costs to run
the line this month.
How much of that
has been met.

The two are not the
same number.

The gap is the part
worth looking at.


Next time you fall —
and you will —
look at the numbers
before you rise.

If the gap troubles
you, you already
know the word.
